newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk police detain over 100 Islam sect members.
newsitem.headline: Turk police detain over 100 Islam sect members.

text.p: Turkish police on Sunday detained around 125 members of an Islamic sect trying to hold a religious service to commemorate a late Moslem religious leader, Anatolian news agency said.
It said 60 members of the Aczimendi sect were taken into custody after one of them made a speech criticising the secular founder of modern Turkey, Kemal Ataturk, at Ankara's biggest mosque, Kocatepe.

Police also arrested three seperate Aczimendi groups, of up to 30 people, attempting to enter Ankara to attend a service at Kocatepe for Bediuzzaman Said-i Nursi, regarded as the spiritual guide of several Moslem sects in Turkey. He died in 1960.
The Aczimendis don long dark cloaks, turbans and carry staffs, making them easily recognisable from the vast majority of Turks who wear Western-style clothing.
Islamic sects are technically illegal in Turkey but authorities often turn a blind eye to their activities.
